title: SFT formatter: trimming, loss-mask spans, role enums
scenario: Chat logs become SFT examples: roles normalised, bad conversations rejected, default system prompt added, oldest turns trimmed to a token budget, and assistant-content character spans recorded for the loss mask.

verified.why_correct: `<=` looks like a boundary slip, but the README says an example of exactly max_tokens fits. truncate uses fits both for the loop and for the final too_long check, so the boundary is consistent.

bugs.title: Assistant span starts on the header newline
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_assistant_spans: c03 spans are [[105, 109], [160, 164]] instead of [[106, 110], [161, 165]]. Every span is shifted one character left (text[s:e] would be "\nCat" instead of "Cat.").
bugs.why: The header is the tag plus a newline. Starting at offset + len(tag) puts the span on the '\n', and because end is start + len(content), the last character of the content falls outside the span.
hints: Print text[s:e] for one span. What is the first character?
Compare how block() builds the header with how assistant_spans skips it.
Skip the newline too: offset + len(tag(message)) + 1.
probes: Why is the span length still right but the content wrong?
How would you compute the span so it can't drift from block()?

bugs.title: Trimming edits the caller's message list
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_truncation: c07 and c13 show turns_dropped 0 instead of 2, while their token counts (20, 26) are already the trimmed values.
bugs.why: kept is the same list object as messages, so `del kept[...]` also shrinks the caller's list. build_examples then computes turns_dropped = len(messages) - len(kept) = 0, since both names point at the trimmed list.
hints: c07 was clearly trimmed (20 tokens). Why does turns_dropped say 0?
What does build_examples compare to get turns_dropped, and what does truncate do to its argument?
probes: Why are the token counts still right?
Would a shallow copy be enough if truncate changed message content instead of removing messages?

bugs.title: Role enum compared with a string
bugs.why: Role is a plain Enum, so Role.ASSISTANT == 'assistant' is False. The count comes out 0 instead of 13.
hints: assistant_turns is 0 although every example has an assistant reply.
What type is m.role? What does it compare equal to?
probes: Would class Role(str, Enum) have avoided this? What would you give up?
Where else in the package are roles compared, and how?

context_qa.q: What does build_examples do for each conversation?
context_qa.a: It runs loader.validate on the cleaned messages (rejecting with its reason), adds the default system prompt with with_system, trims with render.truncate, and stores text, tokens, spans and turns_dropped for the trimmed messages. A None from truncate becomes a too_long rejection.
models.Role is an Enum with values 'system', 'user', 'assistant'. normalize_role lower-cases and trims the raw string, maps aliases through ALIASES, and returns Role(name).

context_qa.q: How does truncate decide what to drop?
context_qa.a: It works on `kept`, starting after the system message, and deletes kept[start:start + 2] while the messages don't fit and more than one pair remains. It returns kept if it fits, otherwise None.
render.count_tokens returns len(content.split()) + 2 per message; total_tokens sums that over the list.

context_qa.q: What does a rendered block look like?
context_qa.a: render.block(m) returns tag(m) + '\n' + content + '<|end|>\n', where tag(m) is '<|' + role value + '|>'. render() concatenates the blocks.

context_qa.q: Which conversations get trimmed with this data?
context_qa.a: c07 (54 tokens before trimming) and c13 (46) are over the 40-token budget and lose their first user/assistant pair. c12 has a single long pair and cannot be trimmed.
